summary: Specifies a way to describe typed relationships between web resources, called link relation types, and sets up a registry for them. It also defines the HTTP Link header field for carrying such links. It was a standards-track specification and was replaced by RFC 8288.

eli5.summary: Web pages can say "this is the next page" or "this is my author". This sets the labels for such connections and a header to send them. A newer document has since replaced it.

questions: what is the http link header
what is rel next in link header

subtitle: Typed links between web resources, a registry of link relation types, and the HTTP Link header.

tldr.problem: HTML and Atom each had their own way to say how one resource relates to another, and the HTTP Link header had been dropped from HTTP/1.1, leaving its status unclear.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines a link as a context, a relation type, a target and optional attributes, sets up an IANA registry of relation types, and re-specifies the Link header field with updated but backwards-compatible syntax.
tldr.outcome: Typed links work independently of the format that carries them. RFC 5988 was obsoleted by RFC 8288.

today: RFC 5988 was obsoleted by RFC 8288, which now defines web linking. It had updated RFC 4287.

sections.title: Why a General Framework for Links
sections.content:
HTML and Atom already let a document say how it relates to another resource, but the two mechanisms are specified separately. Links need not depend on one format, which matters when a resource has representations in several formats. This RFC defines a framework for typed links that is not tied to a serialisation, by redefining the Atom link relation registry with a broader domain and adding the relations HTML defined.

It also deals with the Link HTTP header. That header was defined in RFC 2068 but removed from RFC 2616 for lack of implementation experience. Since then some user agents implemented it, for example for stylesheets. Its unclear status led some to consider minting new headers, so this RFC re-specifies it.
sections.eli5: Instead of every kind of file inventing its own way to say "next page", there is now one shared set of labels and one way to send them.

sections.title: Links and Relation Types
sections.content:
A link is a typed connection between two resources identified by IRIs. It has a context IRI, a link relation type, a target IRI and optionally target attributes. It reads as "{context IRI} has a {relation type} resource at {target IRI}, which has {target attributes}". There is no limit on how many links may exist to, from or between resources, and their order is not significant.

A relation type describes how the context relates to the target, for example copyright. It is not a media type and does not say what format comes back. Relation types should not imply extra meaning from other types or from how often they appear; the one exception is the pair alternate and stylesheet in HTML4.

There are two kinds. Registered types are short names in an IANA registry, compared case-insensitively. They must not constrain the media type of the context or the target. Extension types are URIs, compared as case-insensitive strings, and clients should not automatically fetch them. All-lowercase URIs are recommended.
sections.eli5: A link is a sentence: this page has a "next page" over there. The label "next" tells you the kind of connection, not what the other page looks like.

sections.title: The Link Header Field
sections.content:
The Link header carries one or more links. Each link-value is a target URI-Reference in angle brackets followed by parameters. Relative targets are resolved by RFC 3986 and the message body's base IRI is not applied.

By default the context is the requested resource. The anchor parameter can override it, and a consumer that ignores anchor must ignore the whole link. The rel parameter gives the relation type, must not appear more than once, and later occurrences are ignored. The rev parameter is deprecated because it confuses authors and readers.

The target attributes are hreflang, media, title, title*, type and any extension parameters. hreflang and type are only hints and do not override the real response headers. If both title and title* are present, processors should use title*. Extension relation types in Link headers must be absolute URIs.
sections.eli5: The Link header is a label tag attached to a web response. It says where to go, what kind of connection it is, and can add a nickname.

sections.title: The Registries
sections.content:
The RFC updates the Link header's Message Header registry entry and creates the Link Relation Type registry. New types are registered with a Designated Expert under Specification Required. The template has a name, description, reference, optional notes and optional application data. The expert decides within at most 14 days, and decisions can be appealed to the Application Area Directors and then the IESG.

The initial contents hold many names, including alternate, next, prev, previous, start, stylesheet, self, license, up and payment. Most come from HTML4, Atom and related RFCs.

A second registry, Link Relation Application Data, lets applications attach extra data to relation types, such as hints for browsers archiving a page. Each entry needs an application name, description and default value.
sections.eli5: There is an official list of link labels. To add one, you ask a few experts, and they answer within about two weeks.

sections.title: Security and Internationalisation
sections.content:
The content of a Link header is not secure, private or integrity-guaranteed. TLS with HTTP is named as currently the only end-to-end way to protect it. Applications that automatically follow or trust links from headers should consider the attack vectors, especially links that use anchor to attach a different context.

On internationalisation, target IRIs and anchor values must be converted to URIs for the Link header. Relation types are URIs rather than IRIs to make comparison easier, and they are not expected to be shown to end users.
sections.eli5: A link label can be faked by anyone along the way, so a program should be careful before blindly following it.
